speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly what those episodes feel like and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the description; the position-dependent nature of your spinning sensation is very specific. Have you noticed any new hearing loss, ringing in the ears (tinnitus), or fullness in your ear on the side where these episodes occur?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The clinical picture of sudden, position-dependent vertigo without new hearing loss or other neurological deficits is classic for BPPV. Given your age and concerns, I recommend requesting diagnostic images of a Dix-Hallpike test video to confirm the diagnosis.
